solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beauty getting a little behind covering — hurry up!

parts.note: good looks are physical beauty
a nappy covers a baby's little behind; Americans call it a diaper

explanation.surface: Someone admiring a baby's nappy is told to get a move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little behind' looks like 'slightly late'; it is a baby's small bottom. A NAPPY is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom urging speed is a command to hurry.

clue.text: Master offering choice of old money

parts.note: L (pound) and D (penny) are the abbreviations of pre-decimal British money, librae and denarii
or is the word that offers a choice between two things
L (pound) and D (penny) are the abbreviations of pre-decimal British money, librae and denarii

explanation.surface: A master offers a choice of payment in old coins.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pre-decimal currency, pounds, shillings and pence were written L, S, D; 'choice of old money' is L OR D.
explanation.definitionFit: A lord is a master or ruler, the title for a man in authority.

clue.text: Oven topping off what it does

indicators.note: topping means removing the top, so the first letter of the word for what it does is taken away

parts.note: an oven, or this kind of kiln, roasts things

explanation.surface: An oven is described by its function with the top taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent; 'what it does' points back to the oven, which roasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiln for drying hops is a kind of oven.

clue.text: Daft person to feed chickens perhaps with bit of barley not good

indicators.note: with brings the barley letter into the phrase in place of the dropped one
not good means the letter for good is no longer there, swapped for the barley letter

parts.note: to feed chickens you scatter grain on the ground

indicators.note: a bit of barley is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A dizzy person feeds the hens by tossing a little barley that isn't any good.
explanation.walkthrough: SCATTER GRAIN has its G (good) replaced by B, the first letter of 'barley': 'with' brings in B and 'not good' takes out G.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrain is a disorganised, forgetful person, so a daft one.

clue.text: A nose for advancement

parts.note: a dog's nose for something is its scent, its sense of smell

explanation.surface: Having a nose for things helps you get on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a rise or climb, so advancement upwards.

clue.text: Bid to restrain Norse god's excess

indicators.note: to restrain is to hold in, so the god's name sits inside the bid

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or bid
Thor is the Norse god of thunder; the 's is no letter

explanation.surface: An appeal is made to curb the excesses of a Viking deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an overabundance, a synonym for excess.

clue.text: Man taking beer cold

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A man takes his beer chilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a man's name, the setter's usual way of clueing a forename.

clue.text: Dock worker's less serious fellow

definitions.note: dock worker's here is dock worker is, the 's a link

parts.note: lighter means less heavy in tone
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A dock worker is described as a more frivolous chap.
explanation.walkthrough: A LIGHTERMAN works a lighter, a flat barge that ferries goods between ships and quays.
explanation.definitionFit: The barge operator who unloads ships in harbour is a docks labourer.

clue.text: Cautious about Italian lady — one may be drunk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cautious word goes round the lady

parts.note: chary means wary or cautious
donna is the Italian for lady

explanation.surface: A wary man hovers near an Italian woman who may have had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' suggests the lady is tipsy; it means a wine is something drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: This white wine is something one drinks, so it may be drunk.

clue.text: One seeking information about brand new singer? — hardly

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to brand an animal is to sear its hide
Cher is the long-established American singer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pop star is brand new, and the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new singer? — hardly' is the setter's joke: Cher has been singing since the 1960s, so she is far from new.
explanation.definitionFit: A researcher investigates, someone looking for facts.

clue.text: Eastern potentate investing rupees initially — here?

indicators.note: investing means clothing or surrounding, so the potentate wraps the letter

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish commander or chief

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of rupees

explanation.surface: An oriental ruler puts money into rupees and asks if this is where it happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here?' points the whole clue at a place: Agra, the Indian city of the Taj Mahal, where rupees are spent.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is an Indian city, a place where a potentate might invest rupees.

clue.text: Place at end of flight and take off

definitions.text: Place at end of flight and take off

parts.note: a landing is the level space at the top of a flight of stairs
to strip is to take off clothes

explanation.surface: Somewhere planes come down and go up again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' and 'take off' read as aviation, but the wordplay takes a flight of stairs and taking off clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is where aircraft touch down and depart, matching the whole clue.

clue.text: Second try to come between two old prime ministers is cruel

indicators.note: to come between is to sit in the middle of two things, so the try goes inside

parts.note: Tony Blair and Ted Heath were British prime ministers
Tony Blair and Ted Heath were British prime ministers
to hear a case in court is to try it

explanation.surface: A second attempt to get between two former premiers is unkind.
explanation.walkthrough: The prime ministers are clued by first name, Blair and Heath; 'try' is what a judge does to a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hard-hearted lacks compassion, which is cruel.

clue.text: Extra part of diet male gymnasts perhaps take primarily

parts.note: gymnasts are flexible, so male ones might be supple men

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, picking the opening letter of take

explanation.surface: Gymnasts may take an additional product with their meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietary supplement is an extra item added to what one eats.

clue.text: Fortuitous throw of dice sent back minister

parts.note: a chance event is fortuitous

indicators.note: sent back means the throw word is turned round and read the other way

parts.note: a throw of dice is a roll

explanation.surface: A government minister is returned after a lucky dice game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is the UK's finance minister.

clue.text: Actor following peacekeepers having avoided injury

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the actor goes after the peacekeepers

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces are the United Nations'
John Hurt was an English actor

explanation.surface: An actor trails a peacekeeping force and comes out unscathed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhurt means not wounded, having escaped injury.

clue.text: Press network first for American Football

indicators.note: first means the network comes before the press word

parts.note: a grid is a network of lines
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: A media network leads on the NFL.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press network' looks like a newspaper group; 'first' puts the network before the press word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridiron is a nickname for American football, from the lined pitch.

clue.text: Island clump of trees could be this

definitions.text: Island clump of trees could be this

parts.note: the Isle of Man lies in the Irish Sea
a grove is a small group of trees

explanation.surface: A clump of trees on an island could be a particular kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency; a group of these swamp trees could be on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Mangroves are coastal trees that grow in clumps, often forming islands.

clue.text: Can spare transplanted organ

indicators.note: transplanted means moved to a new place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spare organ is available for transplant surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is an abdominal organ producing insulin.

clue.text: Thank Arabs abandoning outskirts in Middle-Eastern city

indicators.note: abandoning outskirts means the letters at the edges of the phrase are dropped, leaving the centre

explanation.surface: Gratitude to Arabs who leave the suburbs of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Two letters go from each end of THANKARABS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ankara is the capital of Turkey, often grouped with the Middle East.

clue.text: Dental work good in woman getting married

indicators.note: in means the good letter sits inside the bride

parts.note: a bride is a woman on her wedding day

explanation.surface: A bride has fine dental treatment before the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental bridge is a fixed replacement for missing teeth.

clue.text: Never designs original formal attire

indicators.note: original means novel or fresh, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A designer never produces original formal clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening dress is formal wear for night-time occasions.

clue.text: Clothing worn around Loch?

indicators.note: worn around means the clothing wraps the loch letter, like a garment on a body

parts.note: kit is a set of clothing, as in football kit
L is the abbreviation for loch on maps

explanation.surface: A garment worn by people living near a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: Scottish dress worn in the land of lochs.
explanation.definitionFit: The kilt is the Highland garment, so Scottish clothing.

clue.text: Get entangled in crime shamelessly

indicators.note: in signals the letters are found inside the words crime shamelessly

explanation.surface: Someone gets shamelessly caught up in crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To mesh is to become interlocked, like gears, so to tangle.

clue.text: Fishing equipment missing first fishes

indicators.note: missing first means the opening letter of the equipment is dropped

parts.note: anglers wind line on reels

explanation.surface: An angler with incomplete gear still lands some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are a kind of snake-like fish.

clue.text: Bishop has row about instruction that's dubious

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an order is an instruction
a line is a row

explanation.surface: A bishop argues about an instruction of doubtful merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel; it is a LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline case is uncertain, so doubtful.

clue.text: Wrong time to go after mount

indicators.note: to go after means the time letter follows the mount

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: It is the wrong moment to set off after climbing a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tort is a civil wrong in law.

clue.text: Great excitement — it's loud always where sport is played

parts.note: F is forte, loud in music
ever means always
a pitch is a playing field

explanation.surface: Excitement at a sports ground is noisy without letup.
explanation.definitionFit: Fever pitch is the height of excitement.
